sources.entry: Ente - An end-to-end encrypted photo-sharing platform (alternative to Google Photos, Apple Photos). (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker/Nodejs/Go
Ente | End-to-end encrypted photo storage and authenticator

summary.one_liner: Ente is a monorepo for an end-to-end encrypted cloud platform with its Photos, Locker and Auth apps plus the server that powers them.
summary.what_it_does: The repository holds the client apps for iOS, Android, F-Droid, Web, Linux, macOS and Windows, along with the backend server. The README describes three products built on the platform: Ente Photos (photo storage and sharing with face detection, semantic search, collaborative albums and background uploads), Ente Locker (encrypted storage for documents, credentials and notes with emergency access, listed for iOS and Android), and Ente Auth (a 2FA authenticator app). Data is encrypted end-to-end across platforms so the provider cannot read it. The README states the source code and cryptography were externally audited by Cure53, Symbolic Software and Fallible. Self-hosting is possible by cloning the repository, per the README.
use_cases: private alternative to Google Photos or Apple Photos
share photo albums privately with family
store important documents and credentials securely
search photos semantically and detect faces
how_to_run: Clone the repository and follow the self-hosting instructions in the project documentation (the README only mentions that self-hosting is possible)
notable: End-to-end encrypted across all supported platforms, with source and cryptography externally audited
Three apps in one monorepo: Photos, Locker and Auth
Ente Auth is an open source 2FA authenticator described as free forever
Photos offers face detection, semantic search and collaborative albums
caveats: Ente Photos is a paid service with 10GB free storage; Locker is free for up to 100 items
Self-hosting requires cloning the repo and setting up the server, which the README does not detail
